LESSON: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we enjoy reading poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication
2. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression
3. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING
This lesson teaches Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading for Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we enjoy reading poems?
2. How are poems different from stories?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication
2. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression
3. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
